source: Deterministic Gamma-log GLMM fixture cross-checked against MixedModels.jl 5.3.0 and lme4 on 2026-04-29. Updated 2026-10-09 for lme4 2.1-0's estimated-dispersion fix (glmerControl(disp_method = 'moment', disp_dof_correction = TRUE)): rust_reference is the engine's fast-PIRLS (lme4 nAGQ = 0) fit with phi profiled inside PIRLS, and the lme4::glmer row is lme4 2.1.0 (scripts/regenerate_lme4_dispersion_glmm_fixtures.R). The MixedModels.jl row (unit-phi PIRLS) is unchanged.

engines.note: MixedModels.jl fits Gamma GLMMs with unit-phi PIRLS weights and puts theta on the boundary here (theta = 0); lme4 2.1 and the engine profile phi inside PIRLS and reach an interior theta = 0.2207. Fixed effects differ at ~2e-2. MixedModels.jl warns that dispersion-family GLMM results are not yet reliable.

glmer(y ~ 1 + x + (1 | group), family = Gamma(link = 'log'), nAGQ = 0) under lme4 2.1.0 defaults (disp_method = 'moment', disp_dof_correction = TRUE); dispersion is sigma(). The superseded pre-2.1 glmer row (lme4 2.0-1, unit-phi PIRLS weights) was theta 1.673899552748074, beta (1.2525348960238136, 0.25143295704500879), dispersion 0.0052807060501246089, logLik 1.231780136165594.
R package glmmTMB was not installed in the local validation environment.

notes: This compact fixture intentionally uses deterministic positive responses so Rust, R, and Julia can rebuild the same data without relying on language-specific Gamma RNG streams.
glmer is preserved as a drift sentinel because its Gamma dispersion profiling can disagree with the MixedModels.jl-style PIRLS objective; it must not be promoted to the only oracle for this path.
2026-10-09: lme4 2.1-0 moved to profiled-phi PIRLS weights; the engine follows it (theta 0.2207, sigma 0.05161). MixedModels.jl still uses unit-phi weights and remains a documented divergence.
